kernelIdea: Given rationals a < b, the midpoint (a+b)/2 is rational and lies strictly between them — so there are infinitely many rationals between any two.

kernels.l1: Between any two spots on the ruler there is always another spot.
kernels.l2: Between any two numbers you can always find the halfway point. And then you can do it again, forever.
kernels.l3: Between any two fractions there is another fraction — take the midpoint. Because you can repeat this forever, there are infinitely many fractions between any two.
kernels.l4: Given two fractions, their midpoint is a fraction lying strictly between them. Repeating shows there are infinitely many fractions between any two, however close together they start.
kernels.l5: Between any two fractions lies another — their midpoint. Repeating gives infinitely many, so the fractions have no gaps you can point at from inside.
kernels.l6: Between any two fractions lies another. The proof needs both inequalities, and both come from the ordering together with closure.
kernels.l7: Between any two fractions the midpoint is a fraction strictly between them, so the fractions have no gaps visible from inside. Closure is exactly what makes the midpoint legal.
kernels.l8: ℚ is dense in ℝ yet has Lebesgue measure zero and is countable; density and size are independent, and the gaps ℚ leaves are what completeness fills.

kernel: Given rationals a < b, the midpoint (a+b)/2 is rational and lies strictly between them — so there are infinitely many rationals between any two. Density is proved, not asserted.
objectives: Prove the midpoint is rational using closure
